# 244 — PR explainer

*Read top to bottom; the diff is described in reading order at the end.*

*Tier: HIGH, as the spec's own risk tier called it — `home.html` is the IA router file and this
touches the boot order of every parameterized analytics URL (`?token=/?chain=/?pool=`), explicitly
named on NORTH_STAR.md's HIGH list.*

---

## The goal

`audit-app.js`'s 2026-08-06 run caught a page that boots with `React is not defined` and renders
**zero pool cards** on `?token=`/`?chain=` — the sacred SEO/analytics surface every `?token=`,
`?chain=`, `?pool=` URL in the sitemap depends on. It fired once in a contended 83-surface run and
zero times in six isolated repeats of the same surface, which is exactly the signature of a race
condition: not reproducible on demand, real every time the conditions line up, and completely
invisible to "I couldn't reproduce it locally."

## The intuition

One sentence: **a script that reads a global must not be allowed to run before the script that
defines that global has finished running — and "I loaded them in the right order in the HTML" is
not the same guarantee as "the browser will execute them in that order."**

`home.html`'s `<head>` loads React, ReactDOM and the translations bundle as `<script defer>` tags.
`defer` guarantees those three execute in document order, after parsing, before `DOMContentLoaded`
— but only relative to *each other* and to that event. It says nothing about scripts inserted
later via `document.createElement('script')`, which is exactly how `home.html` adds the two
analytics-mode bundles (`PoolDetail.compiled.min.js`, `app.compiled.min.js`). A dynamically
inserted `<script>` is **async by default**: it starts downloading and executing as soon as it
arrives, with zero ordering relationship to the deferred tags. The old code triggered that
insertion from a plain inline script at the *end of `<body>`* — which still runs **during HTML
parsing**, i.e. potentially before any deferred script has even started executing. Whichever
script's network request happened to win decided whether `React` existed yet when
`PoolDetail.compiled.min.js`'s very first line (`var{...}=React,...`) ran.

## What changed and why

The fix does not reorder tags or add a hand-written wait for "React, then ReactDOM, then
translations." It gates the dynamic insertion on `DOMContentLoaded`:

```js
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', bootAnalyticsBundles);
```

`DOMContentLoaded` is defined by the HTML spec to fire only **after every `defer` script in the
document has finished executing, in order**. That's a stronger, more general guarantee than "the
three globals these two bundles happen to read today are ready" — it means **every** `<script
defer>` tag `home.html` has, now or in the future, is guaranteed to have run before the analytics
bundles are even requested. A fix that instead checked `typeof React !== 'undefined'` (or waited
specifically for React/ReactDOM/translations) would have been the item-212 trap: correct for
today's two bundles, blind the moment either bundle starts reading a fourth deferred global.

## What did NOT change

`app.js`/`PoolDetail.js` source, the compiled/minified artifacts themselves, the compile/minify
pipeline, any trust rail, the `__APP_MODE` router's mode *decision* logic, or whether any URL
resolves to analytics mode — only **when** the two compiled bundles are requested changed, never
**whether**. The item-221 `.app-footer` occlusion findings (6, re-confirmed live below) and the
planner-768 P2 (item 235) are untouched, as the spec required.

## The diff, in reading order

1. **`home.html`, the analytics-mode script-injection block (end of `<body>`)**: `addScript(...)`
   calls moved into a named `bootAnalyticsBundles()` function; the call site changed from
   immediate invocation to `document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', bootAnalyticsBundles)`.
   A comment above the block explains the mechanism and cites the HTML spec's `DOMContentLoaded`
   guarantee, so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive why this specific event was chosen.
2. **`test_boot_barrier.js` (new)**: a rendered Playwright test with two source-derived population
   checks (parses `home.html`'s actual `<script defer>` set and the loader block's gating
   mechanism — never a hand-typed list) plus three rendered legs (`?token=`, `?chain=`, `?pool=`)
   that artificially delay React/ReactDOM/translations via `page.route` and assert zero page/
   console errors and correct content.

## Verification (all commands run within the 5-minute foreground timebox)

```
node test_boot_barrier.js                                       → 8/8 passed
node test_min_asset_boot.js                                     → 18/18 passed (both router paths)
node test_smoke.js                                               → 11/11 passed
node test_planner.js / test_protocol_parsing.js / test_qualifier_fix.js  → all green
node audit-app.js --only=grid-token,grid-chain,grid-360,grid-768 → 6 findings, all item-221's
                                                                     pre-existing .app-footer
                                                                     occlusion class; ZERO
                                                                     page-error, ZERO dead-end
```
Non-vacuity: reverting the `home.html` change (via `git stash`) reproduced RED on both the
structural gate check and the rendered `?token=` render (the exact `.pool-card`-never-appears
symptom audit-app.js caught live); restoring gave a byte-identical `md5sum` match and all-green
again. Full trace in `specs/244-notes.md`.

## Deviations worth knowing about

None — the spec explicitly left the barrier mechanism to the builder's choice and named
`DOMContentLoaded` as the example; that is what shipped.

---

## Quiz

1. Why is this item tiered HIGH when the actual code diff is under 25 lines in one file?
2. The `<head>` already loads React/ReactDOM/translations with `<script defer>`, which guarantees
   they execute in order before `DOMContentLoaded`. Why wasn't that enough to protect the
   dynamically-inserted bundles on its own?
3. The fix gates on `DOMContentLoaded` rather than checking `typeof React !== 'undefined'` before
   appending the bundles. What does the `DOMContentLoaded` approach cover that a React-specific
   check would not?
4. The test file simulates the race by delaying three specific files (React, ReactDOM,
   translations) via `page.route`. Does the test claim to have proven the barrier for a global it
   never delays — and if so, how, without a rendered leg for that global?
5. How many `<script defer>` tags does `home.html` have, and how many of them are actually read
   by the two dynamically-inserted analytics bundles at the moment they execute?
